_source: design/04-type-system.md §3.5. CI fails the build on breach.
_packageDtsBytesWhy: Raised to 575 488 B (562 KB) by design/14 W (design/01 §3 row 58, views; 2026-09-01): 574 785 B measured, +21 168 B over the 553 617 the previous line measured, same ceil-to-1 KB rule. Two thirds is one new declaration file, `dist/schema/view.d.ts` (13.0 KB): `View`, `MaterializedView`, `ViewTable`, `ViewSchema`, `AnyView`, `AnyMaterializedView`, the two builders' four stage interfaces, `ViewInfo` / `ViewRuntime` / `MaterializedViewRuntime` and their JSDoc. The rest is `query/types.d.ts` (+2 035 B: the six write entry points becoming return-position sentinels on `Executor` AND `CteExecutor`, plus `refreshMaterializedView`) and `schema/index.d.ts` / `session/handles.d.ts`. This is a SIZE gate, not a type-performance one, and the type numbers say so: headline instantiations 82 073 -> 82 339 on TS 5.9.3 and 133 996 -> 134 339 on TS 7 (+0.32 % / +0.26 % against a 200 000 budget), every per-query fixture within +0.95 %, and every derived metric — per column, per table, per declared relation, marginal per usage, and all three schema-size independence ratios — unchanged to the digit. The one fixture over design/14's +2 % band is `empty` at +3.49 %, which is the library compiled against NO schema and therefore measures exactly "how much does one more source file cost"; it is 350 instantiations, it does not scale with schema size or query count, and two rounds of work took it down from 1 821 (see design/14's W RESULT for the two that paid: `ViewImpl extends TableImpl` was 459 of it and the non-generic stage builder 989). Previously: Raised to 553 984 B (541 KB) by design/13 §5's F3 fix round (2026-08-30): 553 617 B measured, +2 705 B, same ceil-to-1 KB rule. All of it is declaration-file prose and four declarations: `TableCodecMeta.insertableKeys` (the insertable set COPY's default column list now reads, so it and the insert path cannot disagree), `CopyColumn.key`, `PgLikeClient.secretKey` and `PgLikeConnection.connect`/`cancel` (the parts of a `pg.Client` the protocol cancel drives itself, instead of `Client.prototype.cancel`, which reads the deprecated `activeQuery`). This is a SIZE gate, not a type-performance one, and the type numbers confirm it: headline instantiations 82 028 -> 82 073 on TS 5.9.3 and 133 822 -> 133 996 on TS 7 (+0.05 % / +0.13 %, against a 200 000 budget), every per-query fixture and every schema-size ratio unchanged. Previously: Raised to 550 912 B (538 KB) by design/12 §4 F1 (2026-08-29): 549 122 B measured, +11 579 B, same ceil-to-1 KB rule. All of it is `07` §6.1/§6.2's builder-level option methods — `.signal()` / `.timeout()` / `.outsideTransaction()` / `.withExecMode()` on `Query`, `GroupedQuery`, `SetQuery`, `InsertQuery`, `UpdateQuery`, `DeleteQuery` and `PreparedQuery`, 28 signatures with their JSDoc, plus `QueryRunOptions` and the `run` field on five builder state records. They are written out per interface rather than behind one `QueryOptionMethods<Self>` mixin precisely so the TYPE numbers do not move, and they did not: the headline instantiation counts are unchanged on both compilers (82 028 / 133 822), every per-query fixture is unchanged, and the largest movement anywhere in the report is +0.75 % on a schema-declaration arm (55 705 -> 56 124 on TS 7). This is a size gate, not a type-performance one. Previously: raised to 537 600 B (525 KB) after design/12 §4 P merged (2026-08-29): the statement-path gate and the encode-path rewrite added 1 219 B of declarations (537 543 B measured), same rule. Previously: raised to 536 576 B (524 KB) after design/12 §4 D merged (2026-08-29): the docs-found `valuesMany` guard fix and the pg-like seam declarations added 1 758 B (536 324 B measured), same ceil-to-1 KB rule. Previously: raised to 534 528 B (522 KB) at the design/12 round-A integration (2026-08-29): the merged tree measures 533 563 B, which is S's 504 595 B plus B's builder-gap declarations (query/types.d.ts 54 843 -> 72 190 B across B and S together: `$all`, the six join signatures and two laterals, `withRecursive`/`fromRaw`, relation `avg`/`min`/`max`, and 07 §1.3's four handle interfaces) plus K4's schema DSL (`pgDomain`/`pgSequence`/`pgExtension`, the index item options, `partitionBy`/`partitionOf`, `clusterOn`, `t.raw`). Each branch had passed its own raised number; the SUM is what ships, so the budget is set at the merged measurement by the same ceil-to-1 KB rule and ratchets from here. Previous step: raised from 409 600 to 524 288 B by design/12 §3 S, the session layer, measured 377 261 B before and 504 595 B after (design/07 §4.2's ~50 error classes, §1.3's handle interfaces, the src/session, src/observe and src/pooler declaration files). This is a SIZE gate and not a type-performance one: the headline instantiation counts moved +1.9 % over the whole round (80 485 -> 82 028 on TS 5.9.3), inside design/12 §3 B's +2 % band. tools/budgets.json gates the same bytes at 900 KB against design/08 §1.2 and passes; this number is the tighter of the two and still ratchets.

_design04Measured._why: design/04 §3.5's own 'Measured today' column, for an honest three-way print: design-04 / here / budget. design/04's prototype was a declaration-only `src/core.ts`; this harness measures the real implementation.

_measuredWs0._why: design/09 §3.0, `node bench/types/forks.mjs`, measured on the WS0 declaration-only prototype: marginal instantiations per distinct query, identical at 25/100/300 tables and on both compilers. Kept as the WS0 baseline so WS1's additions — left-join nullability, the GROUP BY guard, CTE handles, set ops, `$if` — read as a delta rather than as an absolute. WS1's own numbers are gated above and re-measured by `run.mjs` on every run; see design/09 §3.1.
